text: Third, to build up IP jobs and skills, we launched the Workforce for IP Savvy Enterprises or WISE programme, in partnership with SBF, to help Singapore enterprises acquire new capabilities and skillsets through IP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are also working closely with our stakeholders and partners on the Singapore IP Strategy 2030, looking into the next bound, the next decade, which aims to strengthen and reinforce Singapore's position on the world stage as a global hub for innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More details will be announced on World IP Day, which will take place in April, next month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about enhancing Singapore’s reputation as a jurisdiction for companies to protect and defend their IP when disputes arise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, in fact, is one of our key focus areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2019, we amended the Arbitration Act and the International Arbitration Act to clarify that IP disputes are arbitrable in Singapore, and that such arbitral awards bind only the parties to the arbitration proceedings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, IPOS launched the Young IP Mediator initiative, in partnership with our local Universities, to build up IP mediation experience amongst law students, socialise IP mediation to them at an early stage of their career and to build awareness amongst law students and fresh graduates alike.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to build our capabilities in handling IP dispute resolution, to make Singapore a "go to" place when companies have IP disputes to resolve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Moving on to efforts on our technological transformation, topics which Mr Joshua Thomas and Ms Rahayu had spoken about.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many participants in our Emerging Stronger Conversation on Legal Industry Transformation, and this includes legal professionals, those in practice, academics and law students, I think all have been practically unanimous in highlighting the need for the legal sector to embrace technology and to build on existing platforms and capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have taken on board this feedback and our efforts on this front are multi-faceted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The roadmap was co-developed with more than 95 stakeholders from the industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It charts our vision and our plans to promote innovation, and technology adoption and development for Singapore’s legal industry up to 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Moving forward, we will enhance our efforts to uplift the entire legal sector through technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We understand the challenges faced by law practices, especially smaller firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Technology platforms can have impact on its overheads.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It has to invest time and effort to identify and curate and also integrate technology into their existing workflows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The platform will be designed specifically to facilitate legal workflows from end-to-end.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This sets the platform apart from generic software that caters to workflows of businesses in general or to specific segments or sectors of the business workflow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We envisage that the platform will enable law practices and lawyers to work anytime, anywhere and it will have a single unified user interface for lawyers to access the functionalities – such as case and document management – as part of their existing tools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will also allow lawyers and their clients to collaborate easily on legal matters via a one-stop-shop platform as far as technically feasible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will be able to share documents and jointly work on such documents on this platform and it will also aggregate client communications from various platforms such as MS teams, Slack and so forth, but with the caveat that it obviously has to be something that is integratable and not something that is too archaic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The platform will aim to supplement and support existing legal technology adopted by firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As far as possible, we do not want to have the firms reinvent the wheel and will see the extent which we can integrate the existing system or software that they already have with the platform that we have in mind.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We aim to make lawyers ultimately comfortable with using the existing tools and, at the same time, going onto the platform and adopting these new legal solutions, which we believe will give them a significant boost as they continue to compete on a regional and global stage.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will work with other agencies to explore complementary schemes as well to support small-and-medium firms and avail them to assistance by technology consultants and also job redesign services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Because the firms are on different ends of the spectrum and different parts of this spectrum in terms of readiness for technology adoption.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For that we have the Singapore Academy of Law’s Future Law Innovation Programme or FLIP, which Mr Zhulkarnain spoke about.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While COVID-19 has disrupted some of FLIP’s planned activities such as workshops and networking events, FLIP continued to provide support to the legal community, in particular smaller law firms, through its "Lighten-Up" business process improvement programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This "Lighten-Up" programme seeks to help law firms increase productivity through technology and its own business process improvements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Till date, 20 firms have completed or are going through the programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain and Ms Rahayu also asked about equipping our lawyers and students for the future, including enhancing their exposure to new and developing fields of work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is, indeed, an important area as we look at growing future lawyers for the future economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MinLaw has been supporting our lawyers to strengthen their expertise in key practice areas and markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, MinLaw administers the SkillsFuture Study Awards to support practitioners in obtaining new qualifications in growth areas such as projects and infrastructure, insolvency; and practising law in leading overseas jurisdictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As of 19 February 2021, 134 lawyers and in-house counsel have benefited from the scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, MinLaw runs a number of capability development programmes for lawyers to gain domain expertise and market exposure and knowledge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One example is the China Ready Programme – the first run was completed in 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This helps lawyers to better understand not just laws but also business culture and environment in China, enabling them to work more effectively with Chinese clients and partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are aiming to launch the next run later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This programme complements the Lawyers Go Global programme which provides lawyers with a deeper appreciation of regional demand for legal services, and also connects them with local businesses and legal communities in those jurisdictions on their mission trips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Of course, we have not been able to do that recently but we will continue to do so once we have the opportunity to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to work closely with our stakeholders to support relevant training programmes for legal professionals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Joshua Thomas asked about how we can support law firms to internationalise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Apart from the initiatives I have outlined above, we also have been building networks and strengthening collaboration with key stakeholders and marketing our legal services in key markets in ASEAN, in India, in China and we also look at how we can improve access for Singapore law practices and lawyers in these markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This represents a next phase in our efforts to help law firms internationalise through cross-sector collaboration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, not just cross-border but also cross-sector collaboration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Mr Christopher de Souza mentioned, SLA has contributed to the wider whole-of-Government effort to combat COVID-19 during this pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SLA has had to retrofit and manage vacant state properties, and also contract to manage hotels and other facilities, to provide interim accommodations, such as for persons serving Stay-Home Notices and for Government Quarantine Facilities, the GQF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SLA will continue to work closely with the community and its stakeholders to co-create solutions to optimise the use of state properties so as to derive better value for the state and the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, SLA, working with URA, will engage the public on ideas for the adaptive reuse of State properties at Changi Point, as part of its efforts to enhance the rustic charm of the area.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SLA will also continue to convert under-utilised State land into community spaces such as Yarrow Gardens, which will be used as a 3-G Park.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked about SLA’s steps towards digitalisation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SLA has indeed been moving ahead to digitalise, across multiple domains and services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SLA has digitalised its Temporary Occupation Licences (TOLs) processes from front-to-end.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All TOLs are now issued in electronic format, as well as digitally signed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This saves time and reduces the possibility of a misplaced TOL.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Another area SLA is looking into, and which the Member has pointed out, is conveyancing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Conveyancing has remained a largely manual and paper-based process over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Building on that, SLA has been engaging various stakeholders on the development of a Digital Conveyancing Portal that will provide a fully-integrated, secure, efficient and also a transparent end-to-end conveyancing process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will build up the Geospatial Trusted Centre through the continued provision of data concierge services to even more agencies, and also expand our centralised geospatial training and project services to more agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The full OneMap 3D platform – with its rich and integrated layers of geospatial data – will be made available to businesses and individuals in 2021, this year, with new services that aim to help users in making better decisions, such as drone flight planning and simulation for logistics; immersive property-viewing experiences for real estate; and also barrier-free access navigation and wayfinding for citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One of the most fundamental purposes of the state – any state today – is to hold the fabric of a diverse society – bound up, close it together – to uphold justice and the rule of law.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Without justice and the rule of law, there will only be force and violence, and the fabric of that society will fray.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our founding fathers saw this with the utmost clarity, and today it continues to be a fundamental tenet of the way we govern.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Everything that we do in my Ministry is guided by these principles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have done well so far – levels of trust amongst citizens remains high.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many in the international community continue to see the commitment to the rule of law as one of Singapore’s key distinctions when deciding whether or not to invest in Singapore, whether or not to bring their businesses into Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But this is a mission that we cannot succeed at alone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We can only do so, in partnership with all our stakeholders and, indeed, with all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is on this note that I end my speech by extending our heartfelt thanks to the Members of the Bar, the Judiciary, the wider legal fraternity, as well as the many Singaporean individuals and organisations who have come along side us in pursuing this mission and I look forward to the year ahead, optimistic that with shared resolve we can continue to safeguard this legacy that has been left to us by our founding fathers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On community outreach efforts, earlier he mentioned iLAB and the chatbot that are available for the public to use remotely to find out about legal processes and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I like to ask him whether that chatbot is able to handle members of the public who need to use other languages such as Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as Ms Lim might appreciate, it is not often as easy to deal with matters on iLAB which looks at giving legal advice and outline of the laws and is not easily translatable into different languages all the time.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Chairman, I first thank the Minister for his elucidation on many aspects that his and Minister Shanmugam's Ministry run.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The first is the framework of the legislation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I would say that, as I had said previously, excellent moves, timely, needed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I want to pick up on the point that I made about small landlords because I do feel that some are kept in the lurch and are vulnerable because the depreciation in profit of that tenant is actually felt even more so by the small landlord in the rebate that the small landlord gives to the tenant.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I think there needs to be a level of deftness and nimbleness with which an Assessor assesses whether a small landlord needing this income for rental retirement merits giving a rebate or not.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That is the first point that I would like to make in clarification.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second point – I thank the Minister for his explanation on the IP regime.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My points were really about how we need to be able to protect IP regime in Singapore and how we must have a dispute resolution mechanism in Singapore for IP.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I should declare that I am a practitioner in IP law.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But the third point really is how we can monetise that intellectual property, how we can monetise that invention in Singapore, in the overall scheme of IP protection.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My third and last clarification, Sir, is about the caution with which we should approach the funding or over funding of criminal legal aid.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In 1997, the Law Chancellor, Lord Irvine, in England characterised legal aid as a leviathan with a ferocious appetite, that is, it was sucking up so much money, so much of the government's budget and it lent itself to abuse.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, while I support access to justice for the vulnerable, indeed, I support it greatly, I think we should move towards this gingerly and ensure that there is no abuse of the system, both for the sake of the litigant as well as the overall judicial system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And this includes looking at the tenant's performance, looking at the ability of the tenant's business to pick up thereafter, and take all this into account when looking at the relevant compensation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On IP, I agree with Mr de Souza.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To monetise it and to take advantage of it, I think there are two broad aspects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first is to have a system that is strong, clean, transparent, robust, and as I mentioned earlier, quick.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, it is to develop a framework to look at how we can monetise or value intangible assets, which make up the majority of assets on a given company's balance sheet.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To look at how that can be assessed, it can be quantified and how that can then be used as leverage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think Mr de Souza's points are well taken, and it is precisely for that reason that I have said my Ministry continues to study it, its impact in other jurisdictions, the experiences there, and to be careful to scope it to walk a fine line between the balance of looking at how we can help the indigenous and making sure that the state's resources are best deployed, and that it is not being taken advantage of unfairly.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In relation to the iLAB point that was raised by Member Ms Sylvia Lim, I just wanted to share in my perspective as the Co-chairperson of the Community Legal Clinic.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And needless to say, we take into account that there is a need for residents who do not understand English, and the volunteer lawyers are there to assist them in the various languages.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have one point of clarification for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Currently, I understand that they are also lacking in terms of manpower, there is a constraint there, but at the same time if we are able to open up the scope, that would encourage more people to embrace volunteering in their professions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We certainly encourage lawyers to take part in pro bono services and offer their services.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Anything we can do to promote that area, we will consider.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having said that, the training contract is for the purposes of ensuring that the trainee lawyer comes through to the market and is able to serve and practice in the market.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it may not be feasible to just serve a training contract in the Law Society's Pro Bono Office.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But that can be certainly one factor and one aspect of practice that they can look into.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Murali Pillai, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank the hon Second Minister for Law for his characteristic considered and full responses to the speeches made by the hon Members of Parliament for this Committee of Supply debate for MinLaw.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would also like to express my appreciation to the officers of the Ministry of Law as well as its Statutory Boards for their devotion to duty and executing MinLaw's mission.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I had the privilege of meeting some MinLaw officers recently.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They all expressed the hope that they do not have to be involved in so many Bills under Certificates of Urgency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also hope so too, but I am confident that if the situation demands it, they will rise to the challenge.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
